battle.name: 壬申之亂
battle.brief: 672年天武元年，天智天皇崩于近江宮，皇位繼承生裂。大海人皇子自吉野出發，經伊賀、伊勢、美濃募兵並封死不破道，七月分兵兩路直取近江與大和；瀨田橋一戰近江朝廷主力潰散，翌日大友皇子自縊。卡面羅馬標槍未隨軍東渡，陣上投射靠和弓短矢，破盾靠有鈿長槍。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 壬申之亂爆發於飛鳥時代末期，兩個陣營同屬一個倭王國的政治共同體，實質是王位繼承權的內戰。西面一方以近江宮的朝廷為中心：大友皇子在先帝崩後受群臣推戴登基，實權由左右兩大臣與三名御史大夫組成的合議體掌握，四名重臣（中臣金除外）奉命向諸國派遣使者徵發兵力，兵源以畿內與鄰近諸國的農兵為主，指揮靠御前會議與國司、郡司的徵發文書串接，兵派出動極慢。東面一方以皇弟大海人皇子為首，被後世視為皇太弟派：伊賀阿拝郡司以約五百人參與，伊勢國郡司襄助募兵，美濃的多品治先行起兵、封住不破道，讓東海道與東山道諸國的兵源得以匯入；高市皇子領一軍在積殖會師，紀阿閉麻呂統美濃援軍，村國男依率主力沿山道西進，大伴吹負則在倭京奪取近江朝集結部隊的指揮權。近江朝的核心是蘇我氏與物部氏一系的舊門閥，山部王、蘇我果安、巨勢比、來目鹽籠等分任總帥與國司守，筑紫率栗隈王則拒絕出兵。戰爭自東而西在奈良盆地與琵琶湖南岸之間展開；雙方皆以郡司與豪族為徵發單位，沒有常備軍，也沒有統一的戰役指揮編制，勝負取決於誰能更快把分散的郡兵集結到同一個方向。
countriesEn: The Renshin no ran broke out in the late Asuka period, and the two camps both belonged to the same political community of the Yamato realm; in substance it was a civil war fought over the succession to the throne. The western camp was centred on the court at Omi-no-miya. Prince Karu, later Emperor Kobun, was enthroned after his father's death with the assent of the assembled ministers, and real authority lay with a council made up of the two ministers left and right and three censors-in-chief. Four senior ministers, all but Nakatsukuni no Kane, were sent out to the provinces to levy troops, so that the armed force consisted mainly of peasant militia from the capital region and the neighbouring provinces; the chain of command ran through the ruler's council and through the levying documents of the kokushi and the gunshi, and the dispatched columns moved with painful slowness. The eastern camp was headed by the emperor's younger brother, Prince Ohama, and came to be known as the party of the appointed younger heir: the district governor of Abei in Iga joined with roughly five hundred men, the district officers of Ise helped to raise troops, and in Mino the Tashinaji had already risen and shut the Fuwa road, allowing forces from the provinces along the Tokaido and the eastern mountain routes to be pooled into one force. Prince Takaichi led a column that joined the main body at Tsumie in Iga, Ki no Akahime Maro commanded the reinforcements from Mino, Murakuni no Ooyi led the main advance west along the mountain roads, and Otomo no Fuke seized command of the troops the court had assembled at the Yamato capital. The core of the Omi court lay with the old clans of Soga and Mono. Yamabe no O, Soga no Kaku no Yasu, Kose no Hikomi and Kuramochi no Shigetomo served in turn as commander-in-chief and as provincial governor, while the Tsukushi no tsukasa Kuriuma refused to commit his forces. The war ran from east to west across the Nara basin and the southern shore of Lake Biwa. On both sides the levy unit was the district and the provincial clan; there was no standing army and no unified operational command, and the result was decided by who could gather scattered district levies into the same line in the same direction at the same time.
people: 壬申之亂的決策層極小，關鍵人物分屬兩個陣營。核心是先帝的兩名兒子：大友皇子是先帝指定的皇太子，即位時二十四歲，母系出身側室，在嫡子相続的新制下最缺乏靠山；大海人皇子年長數歲，早年被立為皇太弟，推舉大友為皇太子、自己請求出家退居吉野宮，表面上做出退出爭奪的姿態。起兵之後，東面一方的關鍵人物是高市皇子（其長子），率一軍在伊賀積殖與主力會師；美濃的多品治是唯一在皇子抵達之前就自發起兵、封鎖不破道的人物，沒有他，東海道方向的人馬就不會流入大海人一方；紀阿閉麻呂率美濃援軍解了大伴吹負在倭京的危局；村國男依是主力西進的先鋒統帥；高市軍大領高市縣主許梅在金綱井集結時突然失語，三日後轉為神憑，自稱高市社事代主神與身狹社生靈神，說只要向神武天皇陵奉上馬匹與種種兵器就可護住皇子，這是把兵眾的正當性接到神道上的關鍵一環。近江朝一方，大友皇子主持了六月二十六日的群臣商議，實際合議的只有左右兩大臣與三名御史大夫；山部王掛名總帥，被蘇我果安與巨勢比殺死，果安事後自殺；來目鹽籠以河內國司守身分率軍，卻因打算向不破方向的大海人軍投降而被殺；筑紫率栗隈王以外患為由拒絕出兵，大友皇子密令使者佐伯男暗殺栗隈王的密令因美努王與武家王帶劍侍立而未能得手。物部麻呂在主子自縊時不捨離去，成為舊豪族門閥效忠的象徵。
peopleEn: The circle of decision makers in the Renshin no ran was very small, and the key figures were split between the two camps. At the centre were the two sons of the late emperor. Prince Karu, the heir the late emperor had nominated, was only twenty-four years old when he was enthroned, and his mother came from a concubine's line, which left him the weakest claimant under the new rule of direct father-to-son succession. Prince Ohama, his elder brother, had been appointed heir while still a younger brother, and had himself proposed Prince Karu as crown prince and asked permission to retire as a monk at the Yoshino palace, thus appearing to step out of the contest. Once the rising began, the key men of the eastern camp were Prince Takaichi, the eldest son, who led one column and joined the main body at Tsumie in Iga; the Tashinaji of Mino, the only man to rise and close the Fuwa road before the prince even arrived, without whom the forces of the Tokaido provinces could never have reached Ohama's side; Ki no Akahime Maro, who brought the Mino reinforcements and saved Otomo no Fuke at the Yamato capital; Murakuni no Ooyi, the commander of the vanguard that marched west; and Takaichi no kuni no kami Kore, the head of the Takaichi district force, who suddenly lost his voice while the troops were being mustered at Kinou-kai, and who three days later fell into a divine trance, declaring himself to be the deity of the Takaichi shrine and the living spirit of the Haya shrine, and stating that if horses and all manner of weapons were offered at the tomb of Emperor Jimmu, the prince would be protected. On the Omi side, Prince Karu convened the ministers on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month, but only the two ministers left and right and three censors-in-chief actually took part. Yamabe no O, the nominal commander-in-chief, was killed by Soga no Kaku no Yasu and Kose no Hikomi, and Kaku no Yasu killed himself afterwards. Kuramochi no Shigetomo led the court's army as governor of Kawachi, but was killed for having intended to surrender to Ohama's forces at Fuwa. The Tsukushi no tsukasa Kuriuma refused to send troops on the pretext of foreign attack, and the order that Saeki no O was secretly given to assassinate him could not be carried out because Mino no O and Take-ka no O stood beside the prince armed with swords. Mono no Maro did not leave his master when the prince hanged himself, and became the emblem of the loyalty of the old warrior clans.
kits: 本卡兵器是羅馬標槍（pilum）：半米長的投槍，槍桿中空，槍頭為加重鐵質，捅穿盾面後槍桿即折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。它在前二世紀至前一世紀的羅馬軍團是最標準的投射武器，拋出距離約三十米，落地後難以回收，所以每名士兵攜帶數支，剩餘的留待第二次投射；配套的近戰裝備是羅馬短劍與方盾。這件兵器並未出現在壬申之亂的戰場上：飛鳥時代日本沒有任何羅馬技術流入，戰陣上實際出現的是和弓與短矢（矢長約六十至七十厘米，鏃有石、角、鐵諸材）、全長約二米而槍頭有鈿的長槍、直刀與大刀（唐樣直刃，長約七十至八十厘米）、以及木製或皮製的楯。兵員多無成套甲胄，靠葛布與皮條製成的胸腹護具、頸甲與皮胄抵禦流矢。弓兵在約一百五十米上反覆覆蓋接近中的兩軍，槍手在盾陣之後壓制前鋒，佩刀者負責砍斷槍桿與收拾潰兵。與標槍功能最接近的是郡司手中的長槍：同樣是刺穿即棄的思路，只是大和的槍桿是實心木料而非中空竹節，受力彎曲後仍能回收再用。馬匹數量有限，多作統率、傳令與追擊之用，並非主要衝擊手段。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Roman pilum, a throwing spear half a metre long, with a hollow shaft and a heavy iron head, which snapped off once it had punched through a shield, so that the enemy could only drag himself back behind cover carrying half a spear. In the first and second centuries BC it was the standard missile of the Roman legions; it could be thrown about thirty metres, was hard to recover once it had landed, and so every soldier carried several, saving the remainder for a second volley, while his close-combat kit was the short sword and the rectangular shield. This weapon was not present on any battlefield of the Renshin no ran: no Roman technology had reached Japan in the Asuka age. What actually appeared on the field was the yumi and its short arrows, sixty to seventy centimetres long with stone, horn or iron heads; the yari, a two-metre spear with a socketed head; the straight sword and the tachi, Tang-style straight blades of seventy to eighty centimetres; and shields of wood or hide. Most men had no complete armour, relying on a chest and belly guard of hemp cloth and leather strips, a neck guard, and leather armour to keep out stray arrows. The archers covered the closing formations at a range of about a hundred and fifty metres, the spearmen pressed forward behind the shield wall, and the swordsmen cut down spear shafts and gathered up broken men. The nearest functional counterpart to the pilum was the yari in the hands of the district officers: the same idea of a thrust that is spent on impact, except that the Japanese shaft was solid wood rather than hollow bamboo, so that a bent shaft could still be recovered and used again. Horses were few in number and served mainly for command, dispatch and pursuit rather than as a shock weapon.
tactics: 壬申之亂的戰術是典型的島國山地內戰：先決勝負的是情報與道路控制，其次是誰能讓分散的郡兵在同一時點集結。大海人一方自吉野出發時先燒名張的驛馬宿場，切斷近江朝廷在東國的傳訊節點；入伊賀後取得阿拝郡司的五百人，在積殖與高市皇子的軍會合；抵美濃後由多品治封住不破道，這一道封鎖切斷了東海道、東山道方向可能西上的援軍，同時讓大海人得以自東國直接調集兵力。七月二日軍勢分作兩路，一路趨近江，一路趨大和，讓朝廷無法同時應戰兩面。分兵之後，兩軍在山間以弓矢互射、以長槍與刀接戰；近江朝主力因指揮部步調不一，向美濃推進時停滯，反倒讓村國男依一線連戰皆捷，經箸陵之戰後直逼琵琶湖南岸；倭京方面由大伴吹負奪權後率眾屢敗屢集，以反覆重組的隊形抵住自西面與北面來襲的近江朝軍，直到美濃援軍趕到。接近戰術上還有兩手：一是暗號，兩軍以金字為合語辨別敵我，防止混戰與夜戰中誤傷己方部隊；二是以神道固結士氣，高市社的祝（神官）以神憑下令守社中之道，把中道（橘街道）變成一道防線。七月七日息長橫河開戰，七月二十二日瀨田橋主力崩潰，整場戰爭以正面突破、兩翼包抄與追擊收束，沒有長期圍城，也沒有海上的大規模交鋒。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the Renshin no ran are those of a mountainous island civil war: information and control of the roads came first, and after that the question of who could assemble scattered district levies at the same moment. When Prince Ohama set out from Yoshino he burned the relay station at Nabari, cutting a node of the court's communications with the eastern provinces. In Iga he obtained the five hundred men of the Abei district, and at Tsumie he joined the column of Prince Takaichi. On reaching Mino, the Tashinaji shut the Fuwa road: that single closure cut off the reinforcements that might have marched west along the Tokaido and the eastern mountain routes, while at the same time allowing Ohama to draw troops directly out of the eastern provinces. On the second day of the seventh month the army was split into two columns, one moving toward Omi and one toward Yamato, so that the court could not fight on two fronts at once. After the split, the two forces shot at each other with arrows along the mountain paths and closed with spear and sword. The main Omi army, its leadership out of step, stalled as it advanced toward Mino, and this gave Murakuni no Ooyi's line one victory after another; after the fight at Hashihaka it pressed straight to the southern shore of Lake Biwa. At the Yamato capital, Otomo no Fuke, having seized command, was beaten again and again yet kept re-forming his force, holding off the Omi troops coming from the west and the north until the reinforcements from Mino arrived. Two further measures belong to the approach. First, a password: both sides used the word for gold as a recognition sign, so that friend and foe could not be confused in a melee or at night. Second, the war was given religious legitimacy: the shrine priest of the Takaichi shrine, in a divine trance, ordered that the road of the shrine be held, turning the central road, the road later called the Tachibana highway, into a line of defence. Fighting opened at Yokogawa in Hikari on the seventh day of the seventh month, the Omi main force collapsed at Setabashi on the twenty-second, and the whole war was closed out by frontal breakthrough, envelopment on the flanks and pursuit, with no protracted siege and no large engagement at sea.
data: 可核對的數字不多，但時間與里程相當清楚。內亂起於天武元年（壬申）六月廿四日，即儒略曆672年7月24日，至七月廿三日（8月21日）大友皇子自縊收束，前後約一個月。參與的東國兵源包括伊勢、伊賀、美濃、熊野以及東海道、東山道諸國，明確記錄的單一支軍隊是伊賀阿拝郡司的約五百人。朝廷方面，六月二十六日大友皇子與群臣商議時，御前實際只有左右兩大臣與三名御史大夫，四名重臣被派往諸國徵兵；七月初近江朝主力向不破推進，同時另有一支隊伍經大和方向逼近倭京。距離上，名張到伊賀積殖約三十五公里，積殖到美濃不破約七十公里，不破到近江息長橫河約六十公里，橫河到大津瀨田橋約三十公里，全靠步行一日至一日半的行軍完成，消息則靠驛馬宿場與步行使者。武器尺度亦有參照：長槍全長約二米，直刀約七十至八十厘米，和弓有效射程約一百五十米，矢長約六十至七十厘米；羅馬標槍則長約半米，槍頭加重逾一公斤，拋出距離約三十米。戰後天武天皇於673年2月建飛鳥淨御原宮即位。
dataEn: Few verifiable figures survive, but the chronology and the distances are clear. The rising began on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month of the first year of Tenmu, the year of the water-rat, which corresponds to 24 July 672 in the Julian calendar, and it was closed when Prince Karu hanged himself on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, 21 August; the whole thing lasted about a month. The eastern manpower came from Ise, Iga, Mino, Kumano and the provinces along the Tokaido and the eastern mountain routes; the only single force recorded with a number is the roughly five hundred men supplied by the district governor of Abei in Iga. On the court's side, when Prince Karu consulted the ministers on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month, the ruler's council in fact consisted of no more than the two ministers left and right and three censors-in-chief, while four senior ministers were dispatched to the provinces to levy men. In early seventh month the Omi main force advanced toward Fuwa while another column approached the Yamato capital from the Yamato direction. As for distances, Nabari to Tsumie in Iga is about thirty-five kilometres, Tsumie to Fuwa in Mino about seventy, Fuwa to Yokogawa in Hikari about sixty, and Yokogawa to Setabashi in Otsu about thirty; all of this was covered on foot at one to one and a half days' march, while news travelled by relay station and by messenger on foot. The scale of the arms can also be given: the yari was about two metres in total length, the straight sword seventy to eighty centimetres, the yumi effective to about a hundred and fifty metres, its arrows sixty to seventy centimetres long; the Roman pilum, by contrast, was half a metre long, carried a head weighing more than a kilogram, and flew about thirty metres. After the war, in the second month of 673, Tenmu built the Asuka-kiyomihara palace and took the throne.
cause: 壬申之亂的起因有三層。最表層是皇位繼承：六六〇年代後期天智天皇立同母弟大海人皇子為皇太子，日本書紀稱其為皇太弟；到六七一年天智轉而以己子大友皇子為太政大臣，顯示改立嫡子的意圖。嫡子相続制當時剛剛確立，違背了同母兄弟之間由母系血統與妃嬪位次決定順位的老規矩，而大友皇子出身側室、母系門第偏低，正是最容易被質疑的一環，支持大海人皇子繼承的勢力因此在他退居吉野宮之後迅速聚集。其次是白村江之敗帶來的後果：六六三年百濟復國戰爭失敗後，天智把都城從奈良盆地飛鳥遷到琵琶湖南端的近江宮，在玄界灘與瀨戶內海沿岸修築防禦設施，安置百濟遺民，遷都途中多處失火，豪族與民眾的負擔與不滿一路累積。第三是改革本身的摩擦：遣唐使的連續派遣與唐風化改革在中央與地方豪族之間製造矛盾；此外有學者指出，天智與大海人父子之間可能早有裂痕，萬葉集所載額田王（大海人皇子的妃）與天智往來的和歌，常被解讀為父子失和的遠因。三者疊加，加上天智一病不起、崩於近江宮，權力交接在數日之內失序，而朝廷的合議體早已失去實際功能，戰爭隨即爆發。
causeEn: The Renshin no ran had three layers of cause. The outermost was the succession. In the later 660s Emperor Tenmu had made his younger brother Prince Ohama his heir, whom the Nihon Shoki calls the younger brother appointed heir; by 671 Tenmu had instead given his own son Prince Karu the post of grand minister, showing the intention to pass the throne to his direct heir. The rule of father-to-son succession had only just been established, and it broke with the older custom by which the order among brothers of the same mother was settled by the blood of the mother and the rank of the consort; and since Prince Karu came of a concubine's line and his maternal clan was of low standing, he was the one most easily challenged, so the faction supporting Prince Ohama's claim to the throne closed quickly around him once he had retired to the Yoshino palace. Second came the consequences of the defeat at Baekgang: after the campaign to restore Paekche collapsed in 663, Tenmu moved the capital from Asuka in the Nara basin to the Omi palace at the southern end of Lake Biwa, built defences along the Genkai Sea and the Inland Sea, and resettled the Paekche refugees, and the capital move was accompanied by repeated fires and by burdens laid on the provincial clans and the populace. Third were the frictions of reform itself: the repeated dispatch of envoys to Tang China and the Tang-tinged reforms of the court rubbed against the provincial clans, and scholars have further argued that father and son were already estranged, the poems exchanged between Emperor Tenmu and Hatsuta no O, wife of Prince Ohama, in the Manyoshu being read as a distant cause of the quarrel. Layered on top of all this, Tenmu fell ill and died at the Omi palace, the transfer of power broke down within days, and the council of the court had already lost all real function, so the war broke out at once.
impact: 壬申之亂的結果直接改寫了日本的國家形態，餘波延續數百年。政權方面，大海人皇子於673年2月建飛鳥淨御原宮即位，即天武天皇，近江宮的朝廷連同大友皇子的支持勢力一併瓦解；他隨即實施服制改定、八色姓的制定與冠位制度改定，把大夫以下至初階的位階重新編定，進一步推動中央集權。制度方面，此後到大寶律令制定之前，日本不再有遣唐使前往唐朝，直到文武天皇702年才恢復派遣，而律令國家體制的真正成形也延至八世紀初。社會層面上，蘇我、物部等舊豪族的門閥力量被削弱，郡司與中央的關係被重新編排，飛鳥諸宮與明日香一帶成為新的政治中心。史觀上，這場以皇弟推翻皇太子、由反叛者勝出的內亂在日本史上幾乎沒有先例，被後世視為王位繼承從同母兄弟相爭轉向父子直系相襲的起點；壬申之亂的經過也讓後世重新檢視日本書紀中大友皇子即位說的可信度，成為日本古代史研究長期爭論的焦點之一。
impactEn: The outcome of the Renshin no ran rewrote the shape of the Japanese state, and its consequences ran for centuries. Politically, Prince Ohama built the Asuka-kiyomihara palace and took the throne in the second month of 673, becoming Emperor Tenmu; the Omi court and the whole network that had backed Prince Karu collapsed with it. He at once carried out a revision of the dress codes, established the eight clan colours, and reformed the cap-rank system, redefining the grades from daifu downwards and pushing the centralisation of power further ahead. Institutionally, no more envoys were sent to the Tang court between the rising and the compilation of the Taiho Code; the missions resumed only under Emperor Monmu in 702, and the law-bound state itself did not take its final shape until the early eighth century. At the level of society, the clan power of the old houses, Soga and Mono among them, was broken up, the relationship between district officers and the centre was rearranged, and the palaces of Asuka and the district of Asuka in modern Nara became the new political centre. In historical terms, a rising in which a younger brother overthrew the appointed heir and where the rebel won outright has almost no parallel in Japanese history, and later generations read it as the starting point of the shift in royal succession from rivalry between brothers of the same mother to unbroken line from father to son. The course of the war also forced later scholars to re-examine how far the Nihon Shoki can be trusted on the question of Prince Karu's enthronement, and that remains one of the standing points of contention in the study of ancient Japan.
result: 壬申之亂以大海人皇子一方完勝收場。七月二日分兵之後，村國男依一線在息長橫河、箸陵連戰皆捷，七月二十二日瀨田橋一戰近江朝廷主力大敗，倭京的守備隨之瓦解；七月二十三日大友皇子在近江自縊，蘇我系與物部系的舊臣隨之崩解，戰事在沒有大規模長時間追擊的情況下結束。前後約一個月，雙方投入的兵員總數並無可靠記載，但可以確定的是：近江朝廷的戰役因山部王被殺、蘇我果安自殺等內訌而始終失序，士氣與指揮遭重創；大海人一方靠的是郡司層面的響應速度，以及被封住的不破道所帶來的東國兵源。神道層面的收束同樣重要：高市社的祝以神憑宣布皇子受神護，飛鳥淨御原宮隨後興建，壬申年因而成為日本政治秩序重整的象徵年。六七〇年代之後近江宮不再作都，明日香的飛鳥成為新的中心，律令國家體制的建設自此在更強的中央權力下推動。
resultEn: The Renshin no ran ended in a complete victory for the party of Prince Ohama. After the army was split on the second day of the seventh month, Murakuni no Ooyi's line won one battle after another at Yokogawa in Hikari and at Hashihaka, and on the twenty-second day of the seventh month the Omi main force was routed at Setabashi, after which the defences of the Yamato capital fell apart. On the twenty-third day Prince Karu hanged himself in Omi, the old retainers of the Soga and Mono houses dissolved with him, and the fighting was over without any large or prolonged pursuit. The whole thing lasted about a month; no reliable record of the total number of men committed by either side survives, but what is certain is that the Omi campaign was thrown into disorder from beginning to end by the killing of Yamabe no O and the suicide of Soga no Kaku no Yasu, and that its morale and its command were shattered. The winning side owed its victory to the speed with which the district officers answered the call, and to the eastern manpower that the closure of the Fuwa road had made available. The religious conclusion mattered too: the priest of the Takaichi shrine announced in a divine trance that the prince was under the protection of the gods; the Asuka-kiyomihara palace was built soon afterwards, and the year of the water-rat became the emblematic year in which the political order of Japan was put back together. After the 670s the Omi palace was no longer the capital; Asuka in the district of Asuka became the new centre, and the building of a law-bound state was thereafter carried forward under a stronger central authority.
